title: Bipartiteness passes to induced subgraphs
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set, and suppose $G$ is bipartite, meaning its vertices can be properly colored with two colors so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. Let $H$ be any subgraph of $G$ — a simple graph on the same vertex set every edge of which is also an edge of $G$ — and let $s$ be any set of vertices. Then the subgraph of $H$ induced on $s$, obtained by keeping only the vertices in $s$ together with those edges of $H$ joining two vertices of $s$, is again bipartite.
hypotheses_covered: H is a subgraph of G (H ≤ G)
s is a set of vertices
